newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Nam Fatt eyes Thai resort with purchases.
newsitem.headline: Nam Fatt eyes Thai resort with purchases.

text.p: Malaysia's infrastructure construction concern Nam Fatt Corp Bhd said on Thursday it was proposing to buy two Thai companies which will give the firm a stake in a planned resort in Phang Nga province.

In a statement, Nam Fatt said it proposed to acquire stakes in Petchada Paanich Co Ltd (PPC) and Phuket Long Island Development Co Ltd (PLID) for a total of 14.47 million ringgit through wholly-owned P & N Construction Sdn Bhd.
Under the proposal, Nam Fatt is to acquire a 40 percent stake in PPC for 7.69 million ringgit and a 15 percent interest in PLID for 6.78 million ringgit.
Nam Fatt already has a direct interest of 25 percent in PLID, which would be transfered to P & N at cost.
PPC holds a 42.5 percent stake in PLID.

On completion of the proposed acquisitions, Nam Fatt would have an effective interest of 57 percent in PLID which plans to develop an integrated resort on 1,125 acres (450 hectares) of land, with golf courses, hotels, a marina, theme parks and a business and commercial centre.

The proposed acquisitions were expected to contribute eight million ringgit to Nam Fatt's pretax profit for the year ending December 31, 1996. The company reported a pretax profit of 76.98 million ringgit in 1995.
Nam Fatt shares were suspended from September 12 pending an announcement, with the stock last traded at 8.55 ringgit.
